title: Pre-Trained Language Models as Zero-Shot Tools for Social Science Research
abstract: arXiv:2610.19048v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Record linkage and demographic inference from names are routine demands in social science. Most approaches to these problems require labeled training data that are difficult or costly to acquire. I show that pre-trained language models perform both tasks accurately without requiring task-specific training. For record linkage, I introduce EnsembleLink, an algorithm that uses pre-trained embeddings alongside string-based scorers to retrieve a short list of candidates and then identify the likeliest matches. EnsembleLink matches or exceeds the performance of most prior approaches while generalizing across scripts and formats that those methods are unable to handle. For ethnicity inference from names, I show that large language models (LLMs) achieve up to 83.8% accuracy on U.S. voter files, compared to 78.0% for name-supplemented BISG. translated_abstract: 基于姓名的记录链接和人口统计推断是社会科学中的常规需求。解决这些问题的多数方法都需要标注训练数据，而这些数据往往难以获取或成本高昂。我证明了预训练语言模型无需任务特定训练即可准确完成这两项任务。对于记录链接，我提出了EnsembleLink算法，该算法将预训练嵌入与基于字符串的评分器相结合，先检索出候选名单，再识别最可能的匹配。EnsembleLink的表现与大多数先前方法相当甚至更优，并且能够泛化到那些方法无法处理的文字系统和数据格式。对于基于姓名的种族推断，我表明大语言模型（LLM）在美国选民档案上达到高达83.8%的准确率，相比之下补充姓名信息的BISG方法仅为78.0%。开放权重模型提供了可复现的实现，其准确率接近这些顶级模型。此外，LLM（摘要内容在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文证明预训练语言模型无需任务特定训练即可完成社会科学中的记录链接和种族推断任务，提出的EnsembleLink算法达到或超越现有方法的表现，且大语言模型在美国选民档案种族推断上达到83.8%的准确率，超过传统BISG方法的78.0%。
